html:
The Battle of Buxar was fought on 22 October 1764 in Bihar. The army of the East India Company beat three Indian rulers together. Plassey had been won by a plot; Buxar was won by fighting, and it made the Company master of eastern India.

After Plassey the Company's men had changed the nawab of Bengal twice and made fortunes trading duty-free. Their second choice, Mir Qasim, tried to rule in earnest. He moved his capital away from Calcutta, trained an army in the European way and ended the duties for everyone. War followed in 1763. Beaten, he fled west and joined the nawab of Awadh and the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II.

At Buxar Major Hector Munro had about 7,000 men, most of them Indian sepoys, against some 40,000. The allies did not act together. The Company's steady musket fire won the day in about three hours.

By the Treaty of Allahabad in 1765 the emperor gave the Company the diwani, the right to collect the taxes of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, in return for a yearly payment. Awadh became a paying ally. A trading company now held the richest province of India; the famine of 1770 followed.
